properties.natural_language: A transaction received via P2P must have gas limit <= block gas limit (60M post-Fusaka). Transactions exceeding the block gas limit must be rejected before mempool inclusion.

validation_layers: Gas limit check against block gas limit
reachability.notes: Attacker can submit transactions with arbitrary gas limits via P2P. The new 60M default increases the upper bound for valid gas limits.

properties.natural_language: If a per-transaction gas cap (EIP-7825) is active, each transaction's gas limit must also be <= the per-transaction cap, even if it fits within the block gas limit.

reachability.notes: Without a per-TX gas cap, a single transaction could consume the entire 60M gas block. Coordination with EIP-7825 is critical.

properties.natural_language: After Fusaka activation, the EL client's default gas limit configuration must equal 60,000,000. Operator overrides are preserved.

reachability.notes: Incorrect default after fork could cause validators to produce blocks with wrong gas limits, creating network inconsistency.

properties.natural_language: After a block producer reads the gas limit config, the block header gas limit field must equal the configured gas limit value (60M by default or operator override).

reachability.notes: Internal to block production. A bug here would produce blocks with incorrect gas limits.

properties.natural_language: After filling a block with transactions, the total gas used must be <= the block header gas limit (60M).

reachability.notes: Block builders must respect the gas limit. Violation would produce invalid blocks rejected by validators.

properties.natural_language: The gas limit voting mechanism must converge: the actual on-chain gas limit must monotonically approach the configured target (60M) within bounded time after Fusaka activation.

reachability.notes: Depends on validator adoption. Not directly attackable but misconfiguration could delay convergence.

properties.natural_language: A block received via P2P gossip must have serialized size < 10 MiB (CL gossip limit). Blocks exceeding this limit must be rejected before propagation.

reachability.notes: An adversarial block builder can construct worst-case blocks. CL must enforce the 10 MiB gossip limit to prevent propagation disruption.

properties.natural_language: The worst-case serialized block size under 60M gas must remain strictly below the 10 MiB CL gossip message size limit for all possible transaction compositions.

reachability.notes: If a novel adversarial construction can produce blocks >10 MiB at 60M gas, block propagation would fail, causing missed slots. This is the core security claim of EIP-7935.

properties.natural_language: Existing smart contracts must behave identically under 60M gas blocks as under 36M gas blocks. No contract can observe the block gas limit change in a way that alters its execution semantics.

reachability.notes: Contracts using GASLIMIT opcode or gas-dependent reentrancy guards could behave unexpectedly under 60M blocks.

properties.natural_language: A block received via P2P must have a valid gas limit field that respects the EIP-1559 gas limit adjustment bounds relative to the parent block.

reachability.notes: Adversarial blocks could attempt to set gas limit to arbitrary values. Must validate against EIP-1559 adjustment rules.

properties.natural_language: All commitment bytes received from P2P peers must have length exactly equal to BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT. Invalid lengths must be rejected before deserialization.

reachability.notes: Malicious peers can send arbitrarily sized byte sequences. Length checks prevent buffer overflows and malformed deserialization.

properties.natural_language: All proof bytes received from P2P peers must have length exactly equal to BYTES_PER_PROOF. Invalid lengths must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Malicious peers can send proof bytes of wrong length to trigger deserialization errors or crashes.

properties.natural_language: All cell bytes received from P2P peers must have length exactly equal to BYTES_PER_CELL. Invalid lengths must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Malicious peers can send cell bytes of incorrect length.

properties.natural_language: All cell indices received from P2P peers must be < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. Out-of-bounds indices must be rejected to prevent array/table overflows.

reachability.notes: Out-of-bounds cell indices could cause out-of-bounds access to root-of-unity lookup tables, potentially crashing the node.

properties.natural_language: BLS group element deserialization (bytes_to_kzg_commitment, bytes_to_kzg_proof) must perform subgroup checks. Elements not on the BLS12-381 G1 subgroup must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Accepting points not on the correct subgroup would break the soundness of pairing-based verification, allowing forged proofs.

properties.natural_language: Each field element converted via bytes_to_bls_field() must satisfy value < BLS_MODULUS. Values >= BLS_MODULUS must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Malicious peers can send cell bytes with field elements >= BLS_MODULUS. Without validation, arithmetic operations would produce incorrect results.

properties.natural_language: After all validation and deserialization steps complete successfully, the resulting BLS field/group elements are safe for cryptographic operations (pairing checks, polynomial arithmetic).

reachability.notes: If any prior validation step is skipped or buggy, untrusted data enters the cryptographic pipeline.

properties.natural_language: For batch cell KZG verification, all input sequences (commitments, cells, proofs, cell_indices) must have equal length. Mismatched lengths must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Malicious peers could send mismatched-length arrays to cause index out-of-bounds or incorrect pairing operations.

properties.natural_language: After batch KZG verification returns true, every cell in the batch is guaranteed to be a correct evaluation of the committed polynomial at the claimed coset.

reachability.notes: Relies on KZG binding property. If the pairing check implementation is buggy, invalid cells could be accepted.

properties.natural_language: The Fiat-Shamir challenge r must be deterministically derived from ALL inputs (commitments, cell_indices, cells, proofs, domain separator). Changing any input bit must produce a different challenge with overwhelming probability.

reachability.notes: If the Fiat-Shamir hash omits an input, an attacker could craft cells that pass batch verification despite being invalid.

properties.natural_language: The pairing check must use KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL] as the G2 element. Using the wrong index would break the verification equation.

reachability.notes: Wrong G2 element index would silently break verification soundness.

properties.natural_language: Raw blob input to the encoding pipeline must have length exactly equal to BYTES_PER_BLOB. Blobs with incorrect length must be rejected before polynomial conversion.

reachability.notes: Blob data comes from EL via Engine API. A compromised or buggy EL could send wrong-length blobs. Length must be validated before encoding.

properties.natural_language: After blob_to_polynomial() and evaluation-to-coefficient conversion, the resulting polynomial must have exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB coefficients.

reachability.notes: Wrong polynomial degree would produce incorrect cells that fail verification or recovery.

properties.natural_language: After compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs() completes, exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB proofs must be produced.

reachability.notes: Wrong number of cells/proofs would break data availability sampling expectations.

properties.natural_language: For cell recovery, the number of provided cells must be >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 (50% minimum threshold). Recovery with fewer cells must be rejected.

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could attempt to trigger recovery with insufficient cells. The 50% threshold is the Reed-Solomon minimum for correct reconstruction.

properties.natural_language: For cell recovery, cell_indices must be in ascending order with no duplicates. Duplicate or unordered indices must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Duplicate indices could cause the vanishing polynomial construction to produce wrong results, leading to incorrect recovery.

properties.natural_language: For cell recovery, all cell_indices must be < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB and each cell must have length == BYTES_PER_CELL.

validation_layers: Index bounds and cell length validation
reachability.notes: Out-of-bounds indices or wrong-size cells could cause crashes or incorrect polynomial reconstruction.

properties.natural_language: After successful cell recovery, the recovered polynomial's first FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB coefficients must exactly match the original blob's polynomial representation.

reachability.notes: Incorrect recovery would produce wrong cells/proofs that would fail verification by other nodes, potentially causing data unavailability.

properties.natural_language: After recomputing all cells and proofs from recovered polynomial, the output must be identical to what compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs() would produce from the original blob.

reachability.notes: Recovered cells must be indistinguishable from originally produced cells to maintain data availability guarantees.

properties.natural_language: The polynomial commitment binding property must hold: for any committed blob, there exists exactly one polynomial, and any >= 50% subset of valid cells uniquely determines that polynomial.

reachability.notes: Breaking this invariant would allow data withholding attacks where an attacker commits to one blob but distributes cells from a different one.

properties.natural_language: For polynomial multiplication in recovery, len(a) + len(b) - 1 must always be <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB. This must hold for all valid inputs to the recovery pipeline.

reachability.notes: An adversarially chosen set of missing cells could potentially violate polynomial degree bounds if input validation is insufficient.

properties.natural_language: PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY must be a valid generator of the multiplicative subgroup of order FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB in the BLS12-381 scalar field. All FFT and coset operations depend on this.

reachability.notes: Wrong root of unity would cause all FFT operations to produce incorrect results, breaking encoding, verification, and recovery.

properties.natural_language: The KZG trusted setup parameters (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) must be consistent with each other and with the BLS12-381 curve parameters. Using inconsistent parameters breaks all proof verification.

reachability.notes: Relies on the correctness of the KZG trusted setup ceremony. Not directly exploitable unless the toxic waste was not destroyed.

properties.natural_language: Pectra fork transition must be atomic: all 11 core EIPs (6110, 7002, 7251, 7549, 7685, 7691 on CL; 2537, 2935, 7623, 7702 on EL) must activate together at the fork boundary. Partial activation must not be possible.

reachability.notes: EIP-7600 is Pectra (not Fusaka). Fork activation logic for Pectra is not Fusaka-specific.

properties.natural_language: Pectra activation must occur at exactly epoch 364032 on mainnet. The check current_epoch >= PECTRA_EPOCH must use the correct constant for each network.

reachability.notes: Pectra-specific, not Fusaka. Wrong epoch constant would cause premature or delayed fork activation.

properties.natural_language: Prague (EL) and Electra (CL) must activate at the same slot/block boundary. A mismatch would cause EL and CL to operate under different rule sets, potentially causing consensus failures.

reachability.notes: Pectra-specific. EL/CL activation mismatch would be a critical consensus bug but is not Fusaka-related.

properties.natural_language: All EL client implementations must agree on the default gas limit value (60M) after Fusaka activation. Disagreement between clients on the default value could cause validators to vote for different targets.

reachability.notes: If one EL client defaults to 36M and another to 60M, validators would vote for different gas limits, causing inconsistent block capacities.

properties.natural_language: Node hardware must handle 60M gas blocks within the 12-second slot time. Processing time for worst-case 60M gas blocks must be < slot time to prevent missed slots.

reachability.notes: Adversarial blocks could maximize execution time within 60M gas. If processing exceeds slot time, nodes miss attestation deadlines. Likely classified as high-effort DoS (out-of-scope).

properties.natural_language: After commitment deduplication in batch verification, the weight computation must correctly accumulate random linear combination weights for all cells sharing the same commitment.

reachability.notes: Incorrect weight accumulation after deduplication could allow some invalid cells to pass batch verification.

properties.natural_language: After a transaction is rejected for exceeding the per-TX gas cap, it must not be included in the mempool or any block. The rejection must be final.

reachability.notes: If rejection is not enforced, oversized transactions could enter the mempool and be included in blocks.
